incident-bot: PagerDuty INC1234567 fired for service `dedicated-proxy-us-west1` - elevated 5xx ratio and CPU spike :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: acked and looking into it

devon: i'm oncall, acked

maria: seeing short cpu spikes on proxy pods correlating w/ a canary ramp at 12:03. 92% then back down

alex: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/abcd/proxy-overview?orgId=1&from=now-15m

devon: grabbing pod metrics now

devon: ```
kubectl top pods -n prod | grep dedicated-proxy
proxy-1  930m  200Mi
proxy-2  120m  190Mi
proxy-3  50m   180Mi
```

maria: that 930m looks like the canary pod spiking, likely overloaded by synthetic ramp. NLB healthchecks bounced briefly -> retries -> 5xx spikes reported by our alerting rule

oncall-sre: checking NLB health history and probe logs

oncall-sre: probes show transient 503 from proxy-1 for ~30s starting 12:03:10

devon: looking at logs for proxy-1

devon: ```
# tail -n 50 /var/log/proxy/proxy.log | grep "503"
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z GET /v1/generate 503 "upstream overload" trace=abc123
2026-03-15T12:03:13Z GET /healthcheck 503 "probe timeout"
```

maria: confirm: synthetic canary ramp overlapped with a scheduled autoscaler evaluation causing a momentary mismatch in capacity assignment

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC1234567 acknowledged by devon

devon: canary job id: canary/2026-03-15-12:02 ramped to 150rps in 30s. i'm pausing the canary now

devon: paused canary, scaling kicked in, pod cpu normalized. checking traces for customer impact

devon: no customer-facing traces with loss > 1% in sampled window. SLO dashboards look green

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC1234567 auto-resolved at 2026-03-15T12:04:24Z (duration 44s) :white_check_mark:

maria: filing follow-up to prevent recurrence - propose: stagger canary ramps and add small backoff to probe timeout handling on proxy

alex: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/987 - title: "Transient proxy CPU spike from synthetic canary ramp -> adjust canary cadence and probe settings"

devon: adding note to runbook: if auto-resolve occurs and no customer impact, annotate incident as flapping/auto-resolve and temporarily disable canary until follow-up

lee: handing off post-mortem to morning oncall @alex for follow-up with infra and QA

alex: will take it; will coordinate with infra about probe timeouts and schedule change :+1:

maria: incident closed, monitoring will alert if it reoccurs. thanks all :wave:

pagerduty-bot: Summary: INC1234567 - transient `dedicated-proxy` CPU spike caused by synthetic canary ramp; no customer impact; auto-resolved. Tags: auto-resolve, flapping-alert, proxy
